## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Engine releases

The engine ships as a **version**, not a stream of commits: `ENGINE_VERSION` in
[`version.mjs`](version.mjs) is what a member's stamp records, what an engine
migration's range is written against, and what a pack's `minEngineVersion` is
checked against (`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` §2). This file is the log of
those versions and the evidence behind each.

The version is date-anchored `<day>.<n>` — `60820.1` for the first release cut on
2026-08-20. [`version.mjs`](version.mjs) states the shape and computes the next
one (`nextVersion`); rows 1 to 6 below predate the format and are the plain
counter it replaced.

## What a release is

**A release is the commit that bumps `ENGINE_VERSION`, and a bump is only
legitimate once the live canary rehearsal has passed against the tree being
released** (owner decision, 2026-08-12). There is no tag and no separate release
artifact: the updater clones `main` at its newest bumped ref, so the version lives
in the file the mount already carries and there is nothing to cut, push or forget.

The canary is what makes the snapshot *qualified*. It converges a real adopting
repo — running **its own** vendored worker, the copy a member would run — against
the ref under test, and asks whether that repo still works. The fixture rehearsal
on every PR only tests what someone remembered to model; this is the other half.

input.title: The dashboard does not load: a `node:` import reached the page's graph
input.body:
The published dashboard is a blank screen. The browser reports:

```
Access to script at 'node:path' from origin 'https://missingbulb.github.io' has been blocked by CORS policy:
Cross origin requests are only supported for protocol schemes: chrome, chrome-extension, chrome-untrusted, data, http, https, isolated-app.
```

## Cause

The page is served as raw ESM — `index.html` loads `app.mjs`, the browser follows every relative import from there, and nothing bundles. `packs/claudinite-dashboard/settings-read.mjs` imports `engine/settings-file.mjs`, which imports `node:fs` and `node:path` for its `settingsPath()` disk probe. That reach was added with the settings-file rename (#1252 / #1259); it fails the page's first module load and nowhere else.

## Why nothing caught it

`test/model.test.mjs` pins exactly this property, but over a **hand-maintained list** of "the engine modules the page imports". `engine/settings-file.mjs` was never added to that list, so the pin stayed green while the graph grew past it.

## Fix

- Split the settings-file **names** into a browser-pure module; `settings-file.mjs` re-exports them and keeps the disk probe, so no existing disk-side caller changes.
- Replace the hand-list pin with a walk of the page's real import graph, entered from whatever `index.html` names, asserting no `node:` builtin, no bare specifier, no `require()` and no `process.` anywhere it reaches.

input.body:
Closes #1286

The published dashboard was a blank screen: `node:path` fetched as a script from `https://missingbulb.github.io`, blocked as a cross-origin scheme.

## Cause

The page is served as raw ESM, so the browser follows every relative import from `app.mjs` — including the reaches into `engine/`, which is the design. `packs/claudinite-dashboard/settings-read.mjs` reached `engine/settings-file.mjs`, added with the settings-file rename (#1252/#1259), and that module imports `node:fs`/`node:path` for its `settingsPath()` disk probe. One such import fails the page's **first** module load, and nothing after it runs.

## The fix

The settings-file **names** move into `engine/settings-file-names.mjs`, which touches no disk. `engine/settings-file.mjs` imports it, re-exports all four names and keeps `settingsPath()` — so all ~20 disk-side callers are untouched, and a fielded pack version importing the old path still resolves. The page imports the names module.

## The pin that should have caught it

`test/model.test.mjs` pinned exactly this property over a **hand-maintained list** of "the engine modules the page imports". `engine/settings-file.mjs` was never added, so the pin stayed green while the graph grew past it. That test is retired for `test/browser-graph.test.mjs`, which walks the page's **real** graph — entered from whatever `index.html` names as its module script — and asserts no `node:` builtin, no bare specifier, no `require()` and no `process.` in anything it reaches, plus that the walk still reaches the queue modules at all (so a page that stopped importing the engine can't satisfy it trivially). It fails on the tree before this change and passes after.

## Why no engine release

`engineUpdate` replaces the engine tree wholesale on every converge, before the pack flow runs, so the new module reaches a member with or without an `ENGINE_VERSION` bump — and the pack could never land ahead of it. No canary rehearsal is being claimed. The dashboard pack's own bytes changed, so its version moves to `60823.2` with its `VERSIONS.md` row.

## Verified

- New pin fails on the pre-change tree with `engine/settings-file.mjs imports 'node:fs'`, passes after.
- Full suite: 2662 tests, all green (the `engine-pack-lane-shims` test needs an unshallowed clone; run after `git fetch --unshallow` it passes).
- `check_the_world`: 0 blocking. Work scope: clean.
- The page loaded headless (Chromium) against `serve.mjs`: title renders, no page errors, no failed module requests. The one 404 is `dashboard.config.json`, which only `build-site.mjs` generates and is absent in a checkout.

## Folders touched

```
engine/                    settings-file.mjs keeps settingsPath and re-exports the names;
                           settings-file-names.mjs is the new browser-pure half.
engine-tests/pack_loader/  four corpus fixtures copy the sibling module beside settings-file.mjs.
vendoring/                 the two vendor-set fixtures do the same; the structural-set
                           assertion gains engine/settings-file-names.mjs (the closure walk
                           pulls it in on the real tree unaided).
packs/claudinite-dashboard/  settings-read.mjs imports the browser-pure names; model.mjs's
                           header points at the new pin; pack version 60823.1 → 60823.2 with
                           its VERSIONS.md row; test/browser-graph.test.mjs added and the
                           superseded hand-list pin removed from test/model.test.mjs.
```
